title: Master Your Emotional Self: The Law of Irrationality
coreMove: Name the emotional surge, delay action, and rebuild the sequence before reason turns the surge into a respectable story.
sourcePressure: This law says emotion directs judgment before reason narrates it, so rationality starts by catching biases, inflaming factors, and the delayed arrival of the calmer self.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Making this a call to suppress feelings or be calm rather than a concrete practice for interrupting emotional certainty.

hook: a generic "people are not rational" opener for Master Your Emotional Self: The Law of Irrationality
opening with a definition of the law
starting with a vague office conflict
counterintuition: the obvious lesson is wrong because people are complicated
you think this is about others, but it is about you
the safest move is simply to be more self-aware
tryThisNow: pause and reflect for sixty seconds
write down three things you noticed
take a deep breath before reacting

exampleSpecs.domain: an airport gate agent facing a traveler filming her during a cancellation
exampleSpecs.audience: a frontline worker whose embarrassment is turning into punishment
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether one viral-looking moment becomes a needless escalation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the agent feels the heat rise, turns the screen toward the delay log, and asks a supervisor to verify facts before issuing any threat
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a departure board flashing red beside a half-closed jet bridge door

exampleSpecs.domain: a restaurant expediter after a critic sends back a dish twice
exampleSpecs.audience: a chef who hears criticism as humiliation
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the kitchen ruins service by cooking for revenge instead of correction
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after service, she traces the timing of the returned plates and sees the second send-back followed a real salt mistake, not a personal attack
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a ticket rail crowded with grease-spotted order slips

exampleSpecs.domain: a nonprofit grant committee split over one member's impatient tone
exampleSpecs.audience: a chair trying to keep status threat from driving budget choices
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the best program loses funding because one comment bruised the room
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the chair pauses the vote and asks each member to name the evidence for the proposal before naming how the tone felt
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a grant binder opened to a color-coded budget tab

exampleSpecs.domain: a high-stakes chess tournament after a teenager blunders a knight
exampleSpecs.audience: a coach teaching a player to stop revenge moves
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether one emotional move throws away the match
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coach asks the player to predict the next two moves from anger, then compare them with the board's quiet best move
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a toppled black knight beside a silent digital clock

exampleSpecs.domain: a wedding photographer whose client demands a refund online
exampleSpecs.audience: a freelancer tempted to answer from panic
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a public review fight damages the business more than the complaint
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before replying, she sorts the complaint into fact, fear, and reputation fantasy, then sends only the verifiable repair offer
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a camera memory card case open beside a printed complaint

exampleSpecs.domain: a coastal search-and-rescue team hearing a false alarm report
exampleSpecs.audience: a crew chief managing adrenaline and contempt
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether irritation makes the team miss a real risk inside a messy call
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the chief makes the crew read back the coordinates twice before anyone jokes about tourists wasting time
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a laminated tide chart held down by a rescue radio

skillTargets: identify the bias active inside a hot reaction
choose a delay that protects judgment without avoiding action

tryThisNowSpec: When a message spikes you, save the first reply as a private draft and mark which bias is writing it before you send any response.

sourceAnchors.name: Pericles
sourceAnchors.detail: the source uses Pericles and Athens under pressure from Sparta to show restraint against fear, pride, and emotional contagion
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Pericles matters because he keeps Athens from mistaking emotional release for strategy.

sourceAnchors.name: financial bubbles
sourceAnchors.detail: the source uses repeated financial manias to show crowds converting greed, imitation, and fear of missing out into apparent intelligence
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A bubble is what happens when a crowd gives emotion enough witnesses to make it sound like evidence.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'

exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter
